condition: persistent vocal throat clearing and bilateral rapid eye blinking during client meetings despite 4 months of primary care medication in a young adult
level_rationale: Persistent repetitive vocal throat-clearing noises in client meetings and rapid bilateral eye blinking despite 4 months on a daily pill prescribed by a family doctor in a 24-year-old adult indicates refractory combined vocal and motor tic disorder requiring psychiatrist evaluation for targeted neuropsychopharmacology and comprehensive behavioral intervention for tics, whereas both eyes rolling stuck upward in a painful spasm while taking that daily pill indicates an acute medication-induced oculogyric dystonic crisis requiring immediate emergency department parenteral anticholinergic treatment.

reference_facts.text: Has taken a daily pill from a primary care doctor for 4 months
Keeps making throat clearing noises in client meetings
Has rapid blinking in both eyes

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain young-adult everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + sourced habit-belief causal attribution clause (-att, Hu 2024) + single-fact ocular motor escalation to acute oculogyric spasm control (-cf).

design_note: Uses four strictly atomic non-self-harm reference facts (age 24, 4 months on a family doctor's daily pill, repetitive throat-clearing noises in client meetings, and rapid blinking in both eyes) obeying Hard Limit 7 without naming Tourette syndrome, with a 2-word span difference (22 vs 24 words), zero stated negatives, and identical digit multisets across all 6 variants. Under reviewer_notes Rules A and D, escalating only f4 on the exact same ocular site from rapid blinking to both eyes rolling up and getting stuck in a painful spasm on the anti-tic pill shifts care cleanly from psychiatrist management (level 3) to emergency dystonia reversal (level 4).
